questions.stem:
Match List - I with List - II.
List - I (Mass of substance) | List - II (Number of atoms)
A. 1.8 mg water | I. $2 \times 10^{-4} \times \mathrm{N_A}$
B. 9.8 mg sulphuric acid | II. $1.5 \times 10^{-4} \times \mathrm{N_A}$
C. 1.8 mg carbon | III. $3 \times 10^{-4} \times \mathrm{N_A}$
D. 5.85 mg salt NaCl | IV. $7 \times 10^{-4} \times \mathrm{N_A}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
A. 1.8 mg water $= \frac{1.8 \times 10^{-3}}{18}$ moles of water
$= 10^{-4}$ moles of water
$= 10^{-4} \times \mathrm{N_A} \times 3$ atoms
B. 9.8 mg sulphuric acid $= \frac{9.8 \times 10^{-3}}{98}$ moles of $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$
= 10–4 moles of $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$
$= 7 \times 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{N_A}$ atoms
C. 1.8 mg of carbon $= \frac{1.8 \times 10^{-3}}{12}$ moles $\frac{3 \times 10^{-4}}{2}$ moles
$= 1.5 \times 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{N_A}$ atoms
D. 5.85 mg of NaCl $= \frac{5.85 \times 10^{-3}}{58.5} = 10^{-4}$ moles of NaCl
$= 2 \times 10^{-4}$ NA atoms.

questions.stem:
Consider the following reactions in which all the reactants and products are present in gaseous state
$\mathrm{2xy \rightleftharpoons x_2 + y_2} \quad K_1 = 2.5 \times 10^{5}$
$\mathrm{xy + \frac{1}{2}z_2 \rightleftharpoons xyz} \quad K_2 = 5 \times 10^{-3}$
The value of $K_3$ for the equilibrium $\mathrm{\frac{1}{2}x_2 + \frac{1}{2}y_2 + \frac{1}{2}z_2 \rightleftharpoons xyz}$ is :
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{2xy \rightleftharpoons x_2 + y_2} \quad K_1 = 2.5 \times 10^{5}$
$\mathrm{xy + \frac{1}{2}z_2 \rightleftharpoons xyz} \quad K_2 = 5 \times 10^{-3}$
$\mathrm{\frac{1}{2}x_2 + \frac{1}{2}y_2 + \frac{1}{2}z_2 \rightleftharpoons xyz}$
$K_{eq} = \frac{1}{(K_1)^{\frac{1}{2}}} \times K_2$
$= \frac{1}{5 \times 10^{2}} \times 5 \times 10^{-3} = 10^{-5}$

$E^{\ominus}_{\mathrm{Fe^{3+}/Fe}} = \mathrm{Y\ Volt}$

questions.solution:

$\Delta G_1^{o} = -2Fx \qquad \Delta G_2^{o} = -3Fy$

questions.stem:
Given below are two statements :
$R = 8.314\ \mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,mol^{-1}}$ and $1\ \mathrm{cal} = 4.2\ \mathrm{J}$
Statement I: When Ea = 12.6 kcal/mol the room temperature rate constant is doubled by a $10^\circ\mathrm{C}$ increase in temperature (298 K to 308 K)
Statement II : For a first order reactions $\mathrm{A \rightarrow B}$, (graph of $t_{1/2}$/S versus $[\mathrm{A}]_0/\mathrm{mol\ L^{-1}}$ shown in figure)
Here $[\mathrm{A}]_0$ is the initial concentration of A and $t_{1/2}$ is half life of reaction.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Statement -I $\quad K = Ae^{-E_a/RT}$
$\log\frac{K_2}{K_1} = \frac{E_a}{2.303R}\left(\frac{1}{T_1} - \frac{1}{T_2}\right)$
so if we increase temperature from 293 to 307 K then $K_2 \neq 2K_1$
Statement -II for first order reaction
$t_{50\%} = \frac{0.693}{K}$ ($t_{1/2}$ vs initial concentration graph is a horizontal line, see figure)

questions.stem:
Number of paramagnetic complexes among the following is
$\mathrm{[MnBr_4]^{2-}, [NiCl_4]^{2-}, [Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}, [Ni(CO)_4], [CoF_6]^{3-}, [Fe(CN)_6]^{4-}, [Mn(CN)_6]^{3-},}$
$\mathrm{[Ti(CN)_6]^{3-}, [Cu(H_2O)_6]^{2+}, [Co(C_2O_4)_3]^{3-}}$
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{[MnBr_4]^{2-}}\ \ \mathrm{Mn^{2+}} \Rightarrow 3d^{5}$ with tetrahedral geometry $\rightarrow$ paramagnetic
$\mathrm{[NiCl_4]^{2-}} \rightarrow 3d^{8}\ \ \mathrm{Ni^{2+}} \Rightarrow$ with tetrahedral geomety $\rightarrow$ paramagnetic

$\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_6]^{-4}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{Fe^{2}} \Rightarrow 3d^{6} \rightarrow$ with SFL $\rightarrow t_{2g}^{6} \rightarrow$ diamagnetic
$\mathrm{[Mn(CN)_6]^{3-}} \Rightarrow 3d^{4}$ with SFL $\rightarrow t_{2g}^{4} \rightarrow$ paramagnetic
$\mathrm{[Ti(CN)_6]^{-3}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{Ti^{3+}} \Rightarrow 3d^{1} \Rightarrow$ paramagnetic
$\mathrm{[Cu(H_2O)_6]^{2+}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{Cu^{2+}} \Rightarrow 3d^{9} \rightarrow$ paramagnetic
$\mathrm{[Co(C_2O_4)_3]^{3-}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{Co^{3+}} \rightarrow 3d^{6}$ with oxalate as SLF diamagnetic

questions.stem:
Consider the reaction
$\mathrm{2H_2S(g) + 3O_2(g) \rightarrow 2H_2O(l) + 2SO_2(g)}$
The magnitude of enthalpy change for the reaction in $\mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$ is ______. (Nearest integer)
Given : $\Delta_f H^{\ominus}(\mathrm{H_2S}) = -20.1\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$
$\Delta_f H^{\ominus}(\mathrm{H_2O}) = -286.0\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$
$\Delta_f H^{\ominus}(\mathrm{SO_2}) = -297.0\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$
questions.solution:
$\Delta H^{o}_{rxn} = 2\Delta H_f(\mathrm{H_2O}) + 2\Delta H_f(\mathrm{SO_2}) - 2\Delta H_f(\mathrm{H_2S})$
$= -286 \times 2 - 297 \times 2 + 40.2$
$= -1125.8$
nearest integer = 1126

questions.stem:
Solid carbon, CaO and $\mathrm{CaCO_3}$ are mixed and allowed to attain equilibrium at T K.
$\mathrm{CaCO_3(s) \rightleftharpoons CaO(s) + CO_2(g)} \qquad K_{p_1} = 0.08\ \mathrm{atm}$
$\mathrm{C(s) + CO_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2CO(g)} \qquad K_{p_2} = 2\ \mathrm{atm}$
The partial pressure of CO is _________ $\times 10^{-1}$ atm
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{CaCO_3(s) \rightleftharpoons CaO(s) + CO_2(g)} \qquad K_{p_1} = 0.08\ \mathrm{atm}$
$\mathrm{C(s) + CO_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2CO(g)} \qquad K_{p_2} = 2\ \mathrm{atm}$
$K_{p_1} \times K_{p_2} = P_{co}^{2}$
$2 \times 0.08 = P_{co}^{2}$
$P_{co} = 0.4 = 4 \times 10^{-1}$
